phases.implementation_scope: Create DocId/DocRecord, article bundles, lexical/fuzzy/symbol/diagnostic search, contextual help, source/version metadata, command/property links, scratch examples, migration tombstones, privacy boundaries, CLI access, and hooks for semantic tours. Generate signatures/defaults/ranges from authoritative schemas.

phases.user_visible_result: Users can search and open version-matched offline help from commands, properties, diagnostics, and editor context.

phases.title: Creator Alpha qualification
phases.closure_evidence: Linux/Windows/macOS native artifacts, full journey recordings, source diffs, crash-recovery evidence, accessibility reports, performance distributions, and fresh-user usability results close the phase.
phases.current_code_disposition: Supersede the old MS-03/creator-alpha claims with v1 evidence; retain useful captures and tests only as historical comparison.
phases.explicit_exclusions: No claim that later domain workspaces are complete.

phases.stop_conditions: Stop if the workflow requires hidden developer commands, manual source surgery, or unqualified visible/accessibility behavior.
phases.user_visible_result: An unfamiliar developer can build the public proving game entirely through the permanent Creator loop on all desktop platforms.

phases.title: Meridian Interface Schema and binding generator
phases.closure_evidence: Schema compatibility, codegen determinism, round-trip fixtures, stale binding detection, unsupported-type diagnostics, docs linkage, and ABI layout tests pass.
phases.current_code_disposition: Build on core schemas and Rust reflection; do not infer durable contracts from runtime types or hand-maintain language copies.
phases.explicit_exclusions: No universal dynamic object/value substrate and no claim all languages share one runtime.
phases.implementation_scope: Define values, records, enums, handles, interfaces, commands/events, async operations, ownership/lifetime, errors, capabilities, authority roles, save/network/replay metadata, docs, deprecation, and ABI representations. Generate Rust facade validation and language-neutral conformance fixtures.
phases.stop_conditions: Stop if generated bindings leak implementation types, ownership is ambiguous, or one language becomes semantic authority.
phases.user_visible_result: One semantic API definition generates idiomatic, versioned language surfaces and editor metadata.

phases.title: First-class Luau host
phases.closure_evidence: Conformance suite mirrors Rust semantics; tests cover sandbox escape, reload rollback, memory/time budgets, save/network parity, Web reduction, package stripping, and mixed Rust calls.
phases.current_code_disposition: Introduce a capability-scoped Luau host behind Interface Schema, not direct engine internals.
phases.explicit_exclusions: No per-entity hot callback model and no requirement that Luau block Rust-only projects.
phases.implementation_scope: Implement project modules, strict analysis default, generated bindings, sandbox/capabilities, lifecycle, async mapping, hot reload/restart, source maps, debugger, profiler, package modules, deterministic/barrier rules, server/headless support, stripping, and optional native-codegen qualification.
phases.stop_conditions: Stop if disabling Luau leaves runtime/dependency baggage, scripts can access ambient OS state, or debugger frames lose source identity.
phases.user_visible_result: A creator can add strict Luau gameplay, debug it, profile it, save/network it, and package it with zero cost when absent.

phases.title: First-class C# host
phases.closure_evidence: Conformance and mixed-language tests, Hot Reload/restart matrix, AOT/trimming diagnostics, managed exception/source mapping, package size, Web incompatibility reporting, and flagship clean-room 2D C# fixture.
phases.current_code_disposition: Use generated Interface Schema facades and a qualified .NET host/AOT path; do not embed raw CLR types in Meridian contracts.
phases.explicit_exclusions: No promise of universal AOT for reflection-heavy libraries or arbitrary NuGet compatibility without qualification.
phases.implementation_scope: Implement managed project projection, nullable/analysis defaults, lifecycle, async, component/property integration, debugger, profiler, Hot Reload with restart fallback, self-contained deployment, Native AOT qualification where compatible, save/network/replay/headless parity, and stripping.
phases.stop_conditions: Stop if C# requires a different game data model, silently loses behavior under trimming, or cannot produce actionable cross-boundary traces.
phases.user_visible_result: C# has a professional create/edit/build/debug/profile/package path equal in product quality to Rust and Luau.

phases.title: Mixed-language calls, events, debugging, saves, networking, and replay parity
phases.closure_evidence: A mixed project passes conformance, stress, reload, crash isolation, deterministic replay, server/client, and package stripping tests. Debug traces show boundary frames and semantic calls.
phases.current_code_disposition: Use Interface Schema as the sole semantic bridge and explicit host runtimes.
phases.explicit_exclusions: No promise of seamless instruction-level F11 stepping through every runtime.
phases.implementation_scope: Implement exports/imports, generated proxies, value conversion, async/cancellation, errors, ownership, event routing, batching, deterministic barriers, host isolation, lifecycle/reload ordering, source maps, unified breakpoint/session view, cross-language timeline, save/network/replay descriptors, and packaging.
phases.stop_conditions: Stop if one runtime can corrupt another, cross-language calls bypass capability/authority checks, or data semantics differ by language.
phases.user_visible_result: One project safely combines Rust, Luau, and C# without glue-code copies or mysterious runtime boundaries.

phases.title: Professional built-in IDE core
phases.closure_evidence: Large-file/project latency tests, LSP crash/restart, malformed server response, Unicode/IME, multibuffer edits, external-file changes, accessibility, and cross-platform input tests. External editors receive generated configs/commands.
phases.current_code_disposition: Study Zed heavily but independently implement GPL-incompatible core behavior. Reuse only audited compatible components.
phases.explicit_exclusions: No Zed fork and no remote development requirement yet.
phases.implementation_scope: Implement high-performance buffers/rope, syntax parsing, LSP client orchestration, completion/navigation/rename/refactors, semantic tokens, diagnostics, project/toolchain selection, search, references, editable multi-source result views, command palette integration, terminal/tasks escape hatch, generated-file navigation, and editor state recovery.
phases.stop_conditions: Stop if IDE data becomes project authority, language servers can execute ambient commands, or editor performance fails defined interactive distributions.
phases.user_visible_result: Serious code editing can happen entirely inside Meridian while external IDEs remain first-class.

phases.title: Unified debugger, profiler, test runner, and source attribution
phases.closure_evidence: Tests cover adapter crash, stale source maps, optimized frames, mixed runtimes, server/client sessions, failing tests, profiler overhead, redaction, and large trace storage. One regression is diagnosed from symptom to source.
phases.current_code_disposition: Use DAP/LSP/tool adapters where appropriate; Meridian owns engine/process/entity/source semantics and trace correlation.
phases.explicit_exclusions: No custom debugger engine where mature adapters suffice.
phases.implementation_scope: Implement debug-session coordinator, runtime/host adapters, breakpoints, stack/variables/watch, generated proxy transitions, client/server roles, entity/component inspection, tasks/events/waits, test discovery/execution, source-attributed CPU/GPU/memory/build profiling, timeline correlation, capture/export, and restart recovery.
phases.stop_conditions: Stop if diagnostics cannot identify exact source revision, profiling materially distorts workloads without disclosure, or private data leaks into exported traces.
phases.user_visible_result: Breakpoints, stacks, variables, tests, frame/tick context, and profiler costs appear in one engine-aware workflow.

phases.title: Managed toolchains, build graph, artifact service, and remote-ready boundaries
phases.closure_evidence: Build graph cycle/invalidation tests, lost worker, process crash, corrupt artifact, toolchain rollback, offline bundle, concurrent build, deterministic manifest, and multi-language incremental tests. CLI/editor/CI use one API.
phases.current_code_disposition: Retain current build subprocess/artifact/event foundations; decompose and generalize them.
phases.explicit_exclusions: No mandatory cloud/build farm and no hidden host-tool mutation.
phases.implementation_scope: Implement typed build graph, source/artifact nodes, managed toolchains, provider adapters, process sandbox, logs/progress/cancel, cache keys, worker protocol, reproducible outputs, multi-target products, resource limits, failure recovery, and remote-worker-compatible service boundaries without requiring remote operation.
phases.stop_conditions: Stop if build results cannot be reproduced or traced, remote-ready abstractions slow local builds materially, or tools gain uncontrolled filesystem/network access.
phases.user_visible_result: Meridian installs/pins tools and performs incremental multi-language builds without developers orchestrating Cargo, dotnet, Luau, or platform utilities manually.

phases.title: Package and extension ABI with trust tiers
phases.closure_evidence: ABI/layout/conformance tests across compiler versions, hostile package tests, capability-denial tests, crash/restart, dependency resolution, package stripping, and sample extensions in Rust/C++/Luau or C# as applicable.
phases.current_code_disposition: Build on stable C-compatible ABI, Interface Schema, capability packages, and isolated processes. Keep engine-source modules distinct from stable extensions.
phases.explicit_exclusions: No unrestricted backend/process access and no claim every extension class is sandboxable in-process.
phases.implementation_scope: Implement package manifest, dependencies/features, signed provenance, native C ABI, idiomatic C++ wrapper, managed/script packages, editor panels/tools/importers, isolated worker protocol, capability grants, lifecycle, API windows, migration/deprecation, crash containment, and zero-cost disabled behavior.
phases.stop_conditions: Stop if extension ABI exposes third-party backend types, capability prompts are meaningless, or one bad extension corrupts project authority.
phases.user_visible_result: Projects extend Meridian through versioned packages and explicit trust/capability boundaries rather than patching engine internals.

phases.title: Meridian semantic source control and mvs foundation
phases.closure_evidence: Tests cover dirty external edits, rename/reorder semantic merges, binary assets, crash during operation, conflict recovery, Git round-trip, private game boundary, and no source loss. One two-branch scene/prefab merge is resolved visually.
phases.current_code_disposition: Use Git interoperability and Jujutsu-derived research behind Meridian semantics; do not let agents or UI manipulate raw Git history directly.
phases.explicit_exclusions: No hosted sync/live collaboration yet and no forced replacement of expert Git clients.
phases.implementation_scope: Implement repository discovery, checkpoints, semantic status/diff, operation history, branch/bookmark UX, file/binary/scene/prefab/.mui-aware merge, conflict workspace, undo/restore, ignore/local-state policy, external Git coexistence, and CLI mvs surface.
phases.stop_conditions: Stop if semantic history cannot round-trip through Git, source-control operations bypass transactions, or raw Git object manipulation becomes agent-facing.
phases.user_visible_result: Creators checkpoint, compare, branch, merge, and review project changes through semantic operations without learning Git.

phases.title: AI-neutral semantic agent API, Planning boundary, and Action Governor foundation
phases.closure_evidence: Tests prove Planning cannot mutate, model/self-config/skills cannot escalate, raw Git/destructive actions are absent, remote/public actions require policy, no-change succeeds, provider data scopes hold, and deterministic verification outranks model output.
phases.current_code_disposition: Implement general infrastructure useful without AI; TemperTally/TQF remain a separate non-blocking first-party model/training program.
phases.explicit_exclusions: No first-party model, training pipeline, persistent cloud service, or auto-publication.
phases.implementation_scope: Define structured Tasks, read-only Planning capability, typed tool catalog, semantic plan contract, checkpoints, evidence ledger, experiments, provider/model adapters, trust/provenance classes, prompt-injection separation, independent Action Governor, publication boundaries, audit, rollback, and AI-off zero-baggage behavior.
phases.stop_conditions: Stop if an agent has a privileged backdoor, Governor decisions depend on model persuasion, or AI-disabled projects create AI indexes/workers/network traffic.
phases.user_visible_result: Human tools and optional agents use the same typed inspect/plan/change/verify interfaces with hard capability boundaries.

phases.title: TypeScript first-class candidate lane
phases.closure_evidence: Conformance and representative game tests determine Stable, Preview, or Deferred status. Measure startup, memory, package size, toolchain burden, semantics, and debugging.
phases.current_code_disposition: Prototype provider options such as Bun/JS/Wasm/AOT behind Interface Schema; no single runtime is assumed permanent.
phases.explicit_exclusions: Does not block 1.0 if qualification is incomplete.
phases.implementation_scope: Implement project modules, strict typing, bindings, async, debugger, profiler, reload, package manager policy, native/Web products, headless behavior, source maps, sandbox/capability model, and runtime omission when unused.
phases.stop_conditions: Stop or defer if native shipping needs fragile runtime hacks, semantics diverge, or cost exceeds the user value.
phases.user_visible_result: TypeScript can reach first-class status if its runtime, AOT/packaging, debugging, Web/native, and stripping evidence meet the same contract.

phases.title: Meridian Python compiler/runtime candidate lane
phases.closure_evidence: Language corpus, semantic goldens, fuzzing, sandbox, tracebacks, cross-platform, performance, and Meridian game tasks decide Stable, Preview, or Deferred status.
phases.current_code_disposition: Use Luau as the first backend candidate, not public language authority. Keep the anti-magic language contract.
phases.explicit_exclusions: No dunder protocol, metaclasses, eval/exec, arbitrary wheels, CPython ABI/GIL, or compatibility-at-all-costs.
phases.implementation_scope: Implement parser/type flow, modules, classes/composition, explicit protocols/operators, generators/async, errors, decorators as explicit declarations, standard library, source maps, generated backend, debugger/profiler, sandbox, package policy, versioning, AOT/Web path, and differential tests for intentionally shared Python behavior.
phases.stop_conditions: Stop if implementation becomes CPython recreation, backend details leak into source semantics, or performance requires misleading claims.
phases.user_visible_result: .mpy provides familiar Python-like authoring with Meridian-designed semantics and no dunder/CPython baggage if it proves worthwhile.

phases.title: C/C++ native extension and project-language path
phases.closure_evidence: ABI tests across compilers/platforms, sanitizers, ownership/fuzz tests, crash containment, package stripping, debugger, and upgrade/deprecation tests.
phases.current_code_disposition: Use explicit C ABI representations/opaque handles and generated C++ wrappers. Never promise arbitrary STL/vtable ABI stability.
phases.explicit_exclusions: Full C/C++ gameplay parity is not a 1.0 blocker; stable extension interop is.
phases.implementation_scope: Implement headers/bindings, compile commands/clangd, toolchain projection, incremental builds, debugger launch, lifecycle, errors, memory ownership, async callbacks, packaging, platform conditions, unsafe boundary audit, and sample extension. Prototype direct project-language modules behind the same contracts.
phases.stop_conditions: Stop if ABI relies on compiler-specific object layouts, ownership is implicit, or native code gains undocumented ambient engine access.
phases.user_visible_result: C and C++ can build stable native extensions; full gameplay-language ergonomics graduate only when qualified.

phases.title: Production clustered Forward+ Penumbra baseline
phases.closure_evidence: Representative scenes across target GPU classes, image/perceptual review, timing/memory distributions, shader/pipeline stalls, device loss, dynamic resolution, missing capability fallback, and reproducible captures.
phases.current_code_disposition: Retain current PBR/shadow/IBL/extraction/upload work; promote only after fresh visible and performance evidence.
phases.explicit_exclusions: No deferred vendor-neutral reconstruction framework or frame generation.
phases.implementation_scope: Implement clustered light assignment, material pipeline, specular IBL/BRDF, shadows, HDR/exposure/tonemap, transparency, depth/velocity foundations as independently needed, post stack, pipeline warmup/cache, GPU scene evolution, renderer diagnostics, capture, device recovery, and profile settings.
phases.stop_conditions: Stop if image quality is claimed from structural smoke, lower tiers silently change gameplay visibility, or renderer paths duplicate source semantics.
phases.user_visible_result: Projects render a production-shaped 3D scene with coherent materials, lights, shadows, HDR, post, diagnostics, and scalability.

phases.title: Material/ShaderIr and first-party shader authoring
phases.closure_evidence: Text/graph equivalence, source-map, backend differential, capability, hostile shader, compile-cache, hot reload, Web/native, and material corpus tests. One shader error traces to source and practical fix.
phases.current_code_disposition: Retain WGSL/Naga validation as backend tooling; replace WGSL as permanent source authority.
phases.explicit_exclusions: No unrestricted backend shader injection or promise of every advanced language feature at first release.
phases.implementation_scope: Implement MaterialSource/MaterialIr, ShaderIr, reflection, resource/interface semantics, capability checking, source maps, text frontend, graph frontend, deterministic generation, specialization, package modules, live preview, cache keys, custom pass seam, and WGSL/native lowering boundaries.
phases.stop_conditions: Stop if graph/text become competing authorities, backend types leak, or generated shaders cannot be reproduced and inspected.
phases.user_visible_result: Text and visual shader/material authoring share one typed backend-neutral IR and excellent diagnostics.

phases.title: Automatic performance and scalability governor foundation
phases.closure_evidence: Tests induce budget pressure, oscillation, device loss, missing capability, deterministic profile freeze, expert overrides, and gameplay-critical constraints. Measure optimization labor on proving projects.
phases.current_code_disposition: Build on capabilities, profiler, build products, and subsystem policy seams. Do not centralize subsystem state.
phases.explicit_exclusions: No AI requirement and no claim automatic policy is optimal without workload evidence.
phases.implementation_scope: Implement target profiles, frame/memory/latency budgets, policy inputs, hysteresis, pin/override, degradation priorities, reason traces, last-known-good fallback, profile export/freeze, workload telemetry, and cross-subsystem negotiation API. Begin with Penumbra/runtime/content decisions.
phases.stop_conditions: Stop if policy silently changes authoritative gameplay, flaps, hides quality changes, or each subsystem makes contradictory private decisions.
phases.user_visible_result: Developers declare goals and constraints; Meridian measures and chooses inspectable quality/work placement instead of demanding manual tier construction.

phases.title: First-class 2D runtime and editor floor
phases.closure_evidence: C# flagship project, pixel-art and high-resolution vector scenes, tile-world stress, lighting, physics, Web, mixed composition, accessibility, and disabled-3D dependency stripping tests.
phases.current_code_disposition: Do not implement 2D as degenerate 3D; share backend resources only where the domain remains clean.
phases.explicit_exclusions: No requirement for 3D systems in a 2D-only product.
phases.implementation_scope: Implement continuous 2D coordinates, pixel profiles, sprites/vector/raster, layers/canvases, tile topologies and semantic tiles, batching/atlas, 2D materials/lights/shadows, camera/parallax/resolution, 2D collision/query, animation hooks, mixed 2D/3D bridges, huge tile chunks, and compact editor surfaces.
phases.stop_conditions: Stop if 2D package/runtime carries unused 3D tasks/resources, pixel behavior is unstable, or editor concepts require 3D terminology.
phases.user_visible_result: Meridian builds a polished 2D game through dedicated 2D scene, rendering, physics, lighting, tile, camera, and editor workflows.

phases.title: Cairn rigid-body, query, controller, and field foundation
phases.closure_evidence: Cross-platform deterministic/stable tests, stacked bodies, queries, controller slopes/steps/gravity, field batching, replay, server, device absence, stress, and source-linked diagnostics. Shape of Down-compatible public field workload is sanitized.
phases.current_code_disposition: Retain Rapier wrapper tests/provenance as transitional implementation; stop exposing Rapier types and prepare replacement evidence.
phases.explicit_exclusions: No immediate custom solver rewrite or full vehicles/deformables/destruction portfolio.
phases.implementation_scope: Implement body/shape/constraint IDs, scenes/domains, commands/snapshots, contacts/events, queries, physical materials, controller package, arbitrary-gravity field framework, simulation clocks, save/network/replay semantics, debug draw, profiling, failure/recovery, and CPU/GPU/solver extension seams.
phases.stop_conditions: Stop if physics backend becomes public authority, async results mutate worlds outside barriers, or unusual gravity requires engine patches.
phases.user_visible_result: Games use Meridian-owned physics contracts for bodies, queries, controllers, materials, forces, fields, diagnostics, and deterministic barriers.

phases.title: Wavefront audio, music, spatial, and recovery floor
phases.closure_evidence: Glitch/underrun, latency, device hotplug, long-session leak, spatial fixtures, music transition, offline render, browser/native, headless omission, and accessibility volume/control tests.
phases.current_code_disposition: Remove the marker audio crate and recreate Wavefront with real behavior; no placeholder phase.
phases.explicit_exclusions: No online voice-room identity/transport—that belongs to NET/Collective.
phases.implementation_scope: Implement device/callback boundary, mixer graph, buses/effects, streaming, sample/codec assets, spatialization/HRTF seam, listener/environment snapshots, adaptive music transport/quantization/transitions, voice-device capture boundary, offline render, thread-safe commands, underrun diagnostics, device switch/loss, and package stripping.
phases.stop_conditions: Stop if realtime callbacks allocate/block, audio state is mutated from arbitrary threads, or device loss crashes gameplay/editor.
phases.user_visible_result: Games produce reliable low-latency audio, spatial sound, adaptive music, capture/device recovery, and headless/offline products.

phases.title: Save, player profile, replay, migration, and recovery system
phases.closure_evidence: Power-loss/fault tests at every write stage, downgrade/upgrade, unknown fields, partial cloud conflict, replay determinism, mod add/remove, server ownership, privacy, size/performance, and old-fixture one-shot conversion.
phases.current_code_disposition: Retain current journal/recovery tests; replace provisional minimal format with schema-defined domains and compatibility manifests.
phases.explicit_exclusions: No permanent support promise for every pre-release format and no mandatory hosted cloud.
phases.implementation_scope: Implement save authorities, slots/profiles/world scopes, snapshots+journals, stable IDs, unknown-record retention, migrations, rollback, cloud-provider-neutral sync seam, mod set, language/schema versions, replay input/command/event data, deterministic envelopes, encryption capability, corruption quarantine, and UI/CLI recovery.
phases.stop_conditions: Stop if save writes can corrupt the last good state, migrations are untraceable, or preferences/progression/world authority are conflated.
phases.user_visible_result: Games persist player preferences, progression, world state, replays, and versions transactionally with explicit recovery and migration.

phases.title: Visual gameplay and Behavior IR
phases.closure_evidence: A visual-only proving game, graph fuzz/cycle/type tests, deterministic replay, server/client, save migration, profiling, error recovery, and code refactor/interop tests close the phase.
phases.current_code_disposition: Use typed events/commands/state machines and one Behavior IR; do not create a general graph-shaped imitation of assembly language.
phases.explicit_exclusions: No claim that code is obsolete and no arbitrary hidden script generation as source authority.
phases.implementation_scope: Implement behavior components, event logic, state machines, functions/data, specialized graphs, variables, async/waits, reusable libraries, debugging/profiling/testing, save/network/replay/headless semantics, code/visual interop, source text/visual representation, migration, and safe hot reload.
phases.stop_conditions: Stop if graphs become unreadable low-level plumbing, visual/code semantics diverge, or complete-game claim relies on one toy demo.
phases.user_visible_result: A creator can build a substantial complete game visually when it fits Meridian's high-level systems, with code as a seamless escape hatch.

phases.title: Artus rig, animation graph, retargeting, contacts, and physical handoff baseline
phases.closure_evidence: Retarget corpus, contact/slopes, transition, ragdoll recovery, network character, save/replay, hundreds-of-character LOD, Web reduction, and visual review tests.
phases.current_code_disposition: Create real ANI/Artus implementation rather than marker/spec-only code.
phases.explicit_exclusions: Motion matching/cinematics production depth comes in a later content phase.
phases.implementation_scope: Implement semantic rig, profiles, clips, pose layers, animation graph/state machines, blend/inertialization, retargeting, root motion, IK/contact, physical animation/ragdoll handoff, network/replay representation, editor timeline/graph, source maps, LOD tiers, and contribution debugger.
phases.stop_conditions: Stop if components mutate bone arrays in unspecified order, contacts have multiple owners, or bad poses cannot be traced to sources.
phases.user_visible_result: Characters import rigs/clips, retarget, blend, solve contacts/IK, hand off to physics, and debug final body motion.

phases.title: NAV traversability, artifacts, links, and query baseline
phases.closure_evidence: Bake/update/query correctness, streaming seams, moving platform, dynamic obstacle, deterministic profile, cancellation, corruption, crowd-scale query load, and Web/server tests.
phases.current_code_disposition: NAV owns traversability and routes, not game decisions or behavior.
phases.explicit_exclusions: No game-agent planning/decision logic and no solver choice frozen without benchmarks.
phases.implementation_scope: Implement source facets, build/cook artifacts, stable regions/polygons/links, cost layers, queries, async tasks with barriers, dynamic obstacle/update policy, moving platforms/frames, streaming, save/network route descriptors, 2D/3D support, debug visualization, and diagnostics.
phases.stop_conditions: Stop if navigation mutates gameplay directly, artifacts become source authority, or async completion order changes authoritative outcomes.
phases.user_visible_result: Games build and query stable navigation artifacts for agents, dynamic obstacles, links, costs, streaming, and editor inspection.

phases.title: Bearings game-agent intelligence foundation
phases.closure_evidence: Deterministic decision fixtures, invalid/stale facts, planner timeout/fallback, navigation failure, network authority, save/replay, hundreds/thousands of agents, and source-linked explanation tests.
phases.current_code_disposition: Bearings owns decision/planning infrastructure; NAV owns routes, gameplay owns rules, and ML/LLM use remains optional.
phases.explicit_exclusions: No mandatory generative AI, universal NPC brain, or ownership of animation/navigation.
phases.implementation_scope: Implement typed facts/context, goals/tasks, state machines/behavior trees/planner seam, perception/events, blackboard-like scoped state, utility/priority, squad coordination, async plan publication, save/network/replay, editor/debugger, performance tiers, and extension strategies.
phases.stop_conditions: Stop if opaque planning cannot explain decisions, external content can self-promote to authority, or agent work stalls frame-critical simulation.
phases.user_visible_result: Games author inspectable agent goals, facts, decisions, plans, perception, coordination, and fallbacks using Meridian's world semantics.

phases.title: Client/server roles, replication, prediction, and Multiplayer Product Set
phases.closure_evidence: Network simulation tests for latency/loss/reorder, cheat/malformed input, reconnect, version mismatch, prediction error, deterministic server, save handoff, mod set, and headless package. Runnable artifact: multiplayer proving game.
phases.current_code_disposition: Build on product projection and Interface Schema; do not require duplicated server code.
phases.explicit_exclusions: No hosted backend, fleet orchestrator, MMO sharding, or provider lock-in.
phases.implementation_scope: Implement role contracts, replicated state/events/commands, snapshots/deltas, ownership, prediction/rollback/reconciliation, interpolation, RPC/messages, schema/version compatibility, connection plan, session lifecycle, local test topology, replay integration, security limits, asset/package compatibility, diagnostics, and stripping.
phases.stop_conditions: Stop if clients gain unintended authority, single-player uses a separate gameplay implementation, or compatibility failures are silent.
phases.user_visible_result: One portable project produces single-player, listen-server, client, and dedicated-server products with shared gameplay and explicit authority/presentation roles.

phases.title: Selected official gameplay framework foundations
phases.closure_evidence: At least first-person/third-person/2D or other selected starters build real small games, mix-and-match packages, strip unused systems, survive upgrades, and expose understandable source.
phases.current_code_disposition: Deliver shared/selected foundations before 1.0; do not promise completion of every genre family.
phases.explicit_exclusions: No giant inheritance framework or hidden engine-only privileges.
phases.implementation_scope: Implement composable controllers/cameras/interactions/inventory/abilities/attributes/dialogue/quests/checkpoints/spawning/UI flows as packages over public APIs. Include arbitrary-gravity-friendly controller seams, 2D/3D variants, networking/save/input/accessibility integration, source templates, examples, and extension points.
phases.stop_conditions: Stop if starters fork core APIs, packages cannot be removed, or framework convenience constrains unusual games like The Shape of Down.
phases.user_visible_result: Common game types start from modular first-party systems rather than empty projects or monolithic templates.

phases.title: Breadth integration: mixed-language 2D and multiplayer proving projects
phases.closure_evidence: Fresh-user runs, source/API review, deterministic/network tests, platform artifacts, performance/memory, accessibility, recovery, and upgrade evidence. Failures feed back into owning phases rather than project-local hacks.
phases.current_code_disposition: Use clean-room generic projects and the qualification portfolio, not private game content.
phases.explicit_exclusions: No benchmark cherry-picking or special validation-only engine APIs.
phases.implementation_scope: Complete a polished C# 2D game and a mixed Rust/Luau/C# multiplayer game. Exercise editor, input, UI, audio, physics, save/replay, build, debug/profile, server projection, Web where qualified, package stripping, and documentation.
phases.stop_conditions: Stop if either project needs private engine hooks, duplicated language semantics, or manually edited generated artifacts.
phases.user_visible_result: Separate public projects prove Meridian is not merely a 3D Rust demo engine.

phases.title: Alluvium visual graph and incremental production evaluator
phases.closure_evidence: Graph/text equivalence, cache invalidation, cancellation/resume, generation conflict, stable ID, deterministic corpus, provenance, hostile recipe, memory/performance, and zero-runtime-cost baked build tests.
phases.current_code_disposition: Retain current text recipe/scalar evaluator/CLI/inspector foundation; broaden without making runtime systems subordinate to Alluvium.
phases.explicit_exclusions: No mandatory runtime evaluator and no live authority over terrain/weather/physics/render/audio.

phases.current_code_disposition: Use public generic projects plus private consumer evidence without making either private game irreplaceable.
phases.explicit_exclusions: No release claim can be satisfied by a single private project or isolated subsystem demo.
phases.implementation_scope: Close ten project/journey classes: minimal clean, polished 3D, first-class 2D+C#, mixed language, visual-only, single/listen/dedicated multiplayer, Web shipping, CAD-to-game, mod/package, and failure laboratory. Include The Shape of Down as current private consumer evidence where sanitized.
phases.stop_conditions: Stop if any advertised first-class capability lacks a representative project, a project needs private engine hacks, or failures are waived without scoped expiration/remediation.
phases.user_visible_result: The complete validation portfolio independently proves Meridian's major 1.0 promises together.

phases.title: Release candidate, reproducible artifacts, Stable 1.0, and support readiness
phases.closure_evidence: Independent clean-room reproduction, install/update/rollback, signature verification, platform store/manual-action reports, crash symbolication, source/docs correspondence, package/license audit, long-run smoke, and final human product review.
phases.current_code_disposition: Use explicit development/nightly/preview/RC/stable/maintenance channels and immutable release identity.
phases.explicit_exclusions: No deferred TemperTally model, AGPL fleet orchestrator, reconstruction framework/frame generation, MMO, Marquee, or competitive-leadership program is smuggled into the 1.0 gate.
phases.implementation_scope: Freeze source/toolchains/dependencies/schemas/profiles/docs, produce signed manifests and artifacts, SBOM/notices, platform installers/packages, web artifact, symbols/crash identity, update/rollback, release notes/migrations, source tarball, checksums, support window, incident response, security contact, reproducibility instructions, and deadsignal.works stable docs.
phases.stop_conditions: Stop release for any retained Stable claim that lacks required evidence; reduce scope visibly rather than relabel broken work.
phases.user_visible_result: Meridian ships a reproducible, signed, documented Stable 1.0 with support channels, rollback, known limits, and no open-core dependency.
